We will describe the matrix transformation $T$ that reflects 2-dimensional vectors across the horizontal axis. For instance, [fig-reflect-intro] illustrates how a vector $\xvec$ is reflected onto the vector $T(\xvec)$.

A vector $\xvec$ and its reflection $T(\xvec)$ across the horizontal axis.

If $\xvec = \twovec{2}{4}$, what is the vector $T(\xvec)$? Sketch the vectors $\xvec$ and $T(\xvec)$.

$T(\xvec) = \twovec{2}{-4}$.

$T(\xvec) = \twovec{2}{-4}$.

More generally, if $\xvec=\twovec{x}{y}$, what is $T(\xvec)$?

$T(\xvec) = \twovec{x}{-y}$.

$T(\xvec) = \twovec{x}{-y}$.

Find the vectors $T\left(\twovec{1}{0}\right)$ and $T\left(\twovec{0}{1}\right)$.

$T\left(\twovec{1}{0}\right) = \twovec{1}{0}$ and $T\left(\twovec{0}{1}\right) = \twovec{0}{-1}$.

$T\left(\twovec{1}{0}\right) = \twovec{1}{0}$ and $T\left(\twovec{0}{1}\right) = \twovec{0}{-1}$.

Use your results to write the matrix $A$ so that $T(\xvec) = A\xvec$. Then verify that $T\left(\twovec{x}{y}\right)$ agrees with what you found in part b.

$A=\left[\begin{array}{rr} 1 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp -1 \\ \end{array}\right]$.

We have the matrix $A=\left[\begin{array}{rr} 1 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp -1 \\ \end{array}\right]$. It follows that $T\left(\twovec{x}{y}\right) = A\twovec{x}{y} = \twovec{x}{-y}$ as expected.

Describe the transformation that results from composing $T$ with itself; that is, what is the transformation $T\circ T$? Explain how matrix multiplication can be used to justify your response.

$AA= A^2 = \left[\begin{array}{rr}1\amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{array}\right]$.

If we reflect a vector twice in the horizontal axis, we obtain the original vector. The matrix for the transformation $T\circ T$ is simply $AA= A^2 = \left[\begin{array}{rr}1\amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{array}\right]$.
